key_insight: The paper extends CONES to time-varying convex losses and shows a projected proximal method can trade off regret and movement cost with near-optimal rates under evolving nested constraints.
engineering_relevance: This gives online decision systems a principled way to adapt to changing objectives while limiting actuator movement, energy use, or switching overhead.
method: Projected proximal updates over nested feasible sets
Regret–movement tradeoff analysis for convex losses
Lower bounds for weakly adaptive and anytime regret
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees over horizon T: for convex losses, simultaneous regret and movement cost bounds of O(T^{1-β}) and O(T^β), and for strongly convex losses, O(1) regret with O(log T) movement.
watch_item: These are asymptotic theoretical guarantees, so practical performance may depend on how efficiently projections can be computed for the evolving feasible sets.
paper_title: Convex Optimization with Nested Evolving Feasible Sets (CONES) under Time-Varying Loss Functions
